brief.headline: Russia claims Konstantinovka fall after 260 days; fuel-strike drumbeat
brief.lead: Pro-Kremlin channels uniformly celebrated the claimed capture of Konstantinovka as a gateway to Slavyansk-Kramatorsk, while amplifying a sustained campaign against Ukrainian fuel infrastructure; the mood soured on the home front over gasoline shortages and elite arrests.

developments.title: Channels declare Konstantinovka captured after 260-day assault
developments.body: Multiple channels claimed Russian forces completed the seizure of Konstantinovka, framing it as a first step toward the Slavyansk-Kramatorsk defensive line; Poddubny cited Putin confirming the capture. MoD-attributed figures of 20,100 buildings 'cleared' are unconfirmed, as is the broader claim of 133 settlements and 3,000+ km² taken since year start.

developments.title: Sustained fuel-infrastructure strike campaign touted
developments.body: Channels amplified strikes on Ukrainian gas stations, fuel trucks and postal/logistics hubs, with Kotsnews claiming 150+ gas stations and 100 fuel trucks destroyed in June (unconfirmed MoD-style figures). Two Majors posted footage of hits on the Kryvyi Rih highway and Mykolaiv region.

developments.title: Tokmak market strike blamed on Ukraine, 5 dead claimed
developments.body: At least six channels reported a Ukrainian drone strike on a market in Tokmak (Zaporizhzhia) killing 5 civilians and wounding 18; Two Majors alleged Ukraine also targeted rescue workers. Claims are channel-sourced and unverified.

developments.title: Ukrainian drone waves hit Russian regions; Belgorod deaths reported
developments.body: Channels reported Ukrainian strikes on Crimea, Tula, Bryansk (a bus hit), Belgorod (a civilian killed, power/water disrupted) and Tatarstan. Two Majors relayed a claim that air defenses downed 155 drones overnight — a negative-toned admission alongside the usual interception boasting.

developments.title: Home-front strains: fuel rationing and elite arrests
developments.body: Two Majors reported Novorossiysk fuel stations halting free gasoline sales and rationing by card, framing shortages as 'artificial panic,' and flagged the arrest of a former aviation chief and a general on fraud/embezzlement charges — driving a sharp negative swing in Russia-internal sentiment.

developments.title: Rybar claims Khamenei killed in Israeli airstrike
developments.body: Rybar reported Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei killed in an Israeli airstrike with a state funeral underway, and that the US had warned Iran of Israeli assassination plans. Single-channel and highly consequential if true — treat as unverified.

narrative_watch.title: Konstantinovka as gateway to Slavyansk-Kramatorsk
narrative_watch.body: Channels frame the claimed capture not as an endpoint but as unlocking the next objectives, building expectation of momentum toward the Donetsk agglomeration.

narrative_watch.title: Fuel war framing: 'Ukraine's fuel system collapsing'
narrative_watch.body: A recurring narrative casts Russian strikes as systematically dismantling Ukrainian fuel supply, mirroring — and deflecting from — domestic gasoline shortages.

narrative_watch.title: West decadence/decline montage
narrative_watch.body: Rybar and Two Majors stack items on UK budget shortfalls, French/Japanese rearmament and NATO exercises as a decline-versus-mobilization narrative.

mood_lines.text: Euphoric and uniform — Konstantinovka capture plus advances in Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia dominate; every one of 27 posts positive.
Triumphant tone around fuel-infrastructure campaign and logistics hubs; all 11 posts positive.
Split mood: interception boasts offset by grim Belgorod/Bryansk casualty admissions and drone waves on multiple regions.
Net negative, dominated by rearmament anxiety (France, Japan) and Mideast escalation; sharpened from prior baseline.
Sharp deterioration: fuel rationing, elite arrests, espionage warnings and sabotage offset Putin command-control messaging.
Small but uniformly negative — defense of Belousov against comparisons and jabs at Zelensky's front claims.

flag_texts.title: Ukraine strikes on Russia swings to neutral
flag_texts.body: Sentiment moved 100 points to net zero as interception boasts (155 drones downed) collided with negative admissions of deaths in Belgorod, a bus hit in Bryansk, and strikes reaching Tatarstan and Crimea.

flag_texts.title: West & NATO sours to -47
flag_texts.body: A 46-point negative move driven by France's €436bn budget, Japan's shipbuilding fund, Infineon's chip factory and NATO Black Sea exercises, framed as threatening rearmament — alongside Mideast escalation coverage.

flag_texts.title: Russia internal drops 71 points
flag_texts.body: Domestic mood cratered on Novorossiysk fuel rationing, gasoline shortage 'panic,' arrests of a former aviation chief and general, Apple espionage warnings, and a sabotage blast injuring a Rylsk official.

flag_texts.title: Mobilisation chatter across three channels
flag_texts.body: Three channels touched mobilisation themes — Rybar on Ukraine-Germany talks to return draft-age men abroad, Sladkov+ on 2014 militia units formalized as a division, and Poddubny on new anti-drone ammunition — though none signaled fresh Russian call-up moves.

flag_texts.title: No criticism of Putin
flag_texts.body: Direct criticism of Putin was absent; the few criticism posts defended Defense Minister Belousov and attacked Zelensky, while Putin was portrayed as personally directing the Konstantinovka operation.
